text:
michael: quick follow-up to the transport RFC — should we formalize a single pluggable transport across py/ts/go so retries, timeouts and pagination behave the same? curious about ergonomics + long-term refactor risk.

sophia: yes to pluggable interface. avoids duplication. main question: surface sync vs async primitives. TS has async iterators, py has iterators+async, go has channels.

deepak: agree. propose a minimal core: request/stream/paginate. keep idempotency key + per-request hints for retry.

jen: two concerns: 1) streaming backpressure differences, 2) pagination shape (cursor token vs iterator). both affect client ergonomics.

michael: rough TS sketch I was thinking:
```ts
interface Transport {
  request(req: Request): Promise<Response>
  stream(req: Request): AsyncIterable<StreamChunk>
  paginate(req: PaginateRequest): AsyncIterable<Page>
}
```
This gives a single surface for higher-level SDK layers.

sophia: looks good. for Python we should expose: `client.request()`, `client.stream()` returns async generator, and `client.pages()` returns iterator. keep sync wrappers for convenience.

deepak: for Go: `Request(ctx, req) (resp, err)`, `Stream(ctx, req) (<-chan Chunk, <-chan error)`, `Paginate(ctx, req) <-chan Page`. idiomatic.

jen: how do we unify retry semantics? naive approach: transport handles transient retries with exponential backoff + jitter, but caller can opt-out. We need idempotency guarantees for non-idempotent endpoints.

michael: propose default policy: automatic retry for safe idempotent operations (GET-like generation with idempotency key absent?), for generation endpoints require explicit idempotency key for automatic retry. else fail-fast.

sophia: implement backoff params: maxAttempts, baseMs, maxMs, jitter: boolean. expose a RetryPolicy object that SDK layers can pass.

deepak: also consider a retry window for duplicate suppression at the server edge. If client resends due to timeout, server can dedupe using idempotency key. note for private/on-prem customers HSM keys might rotate so idempotency must be client-provided.

jen: pagination: two orthogonal APIs: token-style (opaque cursor) and iterator-style. Iterator should handle auto-fetching pages and converting items into a continuous stream for user. Token-style required for resume/analytics.

michael: agreed. design: PaginateRequest { page_token?: string, page_size?: number, raw?: boolean } Transport.paginate returns pages; SDK layer can wrap into item-level async iterator.

sophia: edgecases: 1) mixed streaming + pagination (e.g., partial pages then stream rest) 2) early cancellation/backpressure: ensure stream aborts cancel inflight requests.

ops-bot: deploy-check: lint + typegen should enforce transport signature parity across languages.

deepak: metric hooks: transport should emit events for request_start/request_retry/request_end with labels: model, route, retry_count, http_status, duration. necessary for cost and perf debugging.

jen: security: transport must accept an injected credential provider to support KMS/HSM signing in Private. avoid baking creds into transport impls.

michael: decision draft from thread:
- implement pluggable Transport interface in TS/Py/Go with request/stream/paginate primitives
- default retry policy: safe auto-retry only with explicit idempotency key for mutating endpoints
- expose RetryPolicy configuration and per-request hints
- provide both token-style pagination and iterator convenience wrappers
- ensure stream cancellation cancels inflight network ops
- instrument transport events for observability

jen: +1 for draft. Can you open a tiny RFC PR with the TS interface + Python/Go mapping and the retry/doc examples?

michael: will do. I'll include small examples and migration notes. tagging @deepak for infra implications.

deepak: will review. will add server dedupe note for idempotency keys.

sophia: i'll prototype the Python async iterator wrapper. will post a short demo snippet in the PR. :rocket:
